body: The radio test sheet says the signal dropped at the tower; the technician’s note asks the field crew to check power before changing equipment.
title: A signal sent for testing

body:
Personal service note: dish three on tower two relayed moisture readings from the trial plots. The signal vanished during the night application, before any public emergency traffic.

The small ordinary expense was the part I could still account for. I could not make the other figure on this page match what I had seen.

I thought someone would ask for this at the gate. They asked instead how many were in the car, and let the paper stay in my hand.
title: Dish three carried plot readings

body:
Torn meter log: near six gigahertz, power dipped as the spraying crew entered the eastern field. The station batteries were full and no storm was recorded.

I folded the corner so I could find the entry again. Someone wanted the book put away before I had even finished copying it.

When I returned, the window was closed and the board was blank. I kept the page because it was the only one with our address.
title: Power dip during the field pass

body:
Letter draft: ask headquarters to compare the Lexington receiver with two leaf samples. The samples carry the same gray film found inside the tower cabinet.

The person who handed this to me asked me to keep the date. I did, though the next version left that day out entirely.

When I returned, the window was closed and the board was blank. I kept the page because it was the only one with our address.
title: Test request with samples attached

body:
Photograph back at the sun mark: the crop-weather receiver is lit, but its plot channel reads blank. The operator noted a chemical smell inside the cabinet.

I carried it home because there was nowhere open to return it. The mark did not come off when I tried to wash my hands.

When I returned, the window was closed and the board was blank. I kept the page because it was the only one with our address.
title: Sun mark over the crop receiver

body:
Technician’s notebook: the cross marks the receiver used for crop-weather telemetry. It failed whenever the treated field pump ran, then recovered after the pump stopped.

We kept one copy for ourselves. The person collecting the other one said the numbers would be corrected later, once everyone had moved.

Someone had to finish the household list even though the office had closed. I wrote the names in the space left for expenses.
title: Cross placed over the test receiver
